title: Co-Founder Equity Split Dilemma
desc: Your co-founder demands an immediate 50/50 equity split with NO vesting schedule, insisting that true founders trust each other completely.

A.title: Agree 50/50 without Vesting
A.log: You agreed to an immediate 50/50 equity split without vesting. The co-founder is satisfied, but future investors will raise serious governance concerns.

B.title: Insist on 4-Year Vesting with 1-Year Cliff
B.log: You stood firm on a professional 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff. Minor tension ensued, but the startup's cap table is protected.

title: MVP Launch: Speed vs Quality
desc: The MVP is ready but contains minor technical bugs. Marketing urges an immediate launch to capture hype; the CTO insists on delaying 2 weeks to refactor.

A.title: Launch Immediately (Fast & Buggy)
A.log: Launched the MVP immediately! Generated +$3,500 MRR, but accumulated +25% tech debt and early customer churn spiked.

B.title: Delay 2 Weeks & Polish Codebase
B.log: Delayed the launch and stabilized the core codebase. Spent $2,000 runway, but customer satisfaction and retention are rock-solid.

title: The Toxic High Performer
desc: Your top growth engineer is crushing customer acquisition numbers, but repeatedly bullies junior team members, triggering resignation threats.

A.title: Keep Them for Growth Metrics
A.log: Kept the toxic engineer to hit growth targets. Revenue rose, but team morale plummeted and culture suffered severe damage.

B.title: Fire Immediately to Protect Culture
B.log: Fired the toxic engineer on the spot. The team rallied behind your principled leadership with a massive +30% morale boost.

title: Server Crash on Major Campaign Day
desc: Due to accumulated tech debt, the primary database servers crashed just as a major tech publication featured your product.

A.title: Issue Transparent Public Apology & Credits
A.log: Published an honest post-mortem and refunded affected users. The transparency turned an outage into a public relations triumph.

B.title: Claim Scheduled Routine Maintenance
B.log: Blamed the outage on routine maintenance. Tech-savvy users caught the deception, doubling churn on social channels.

title: Predatory VC Term Sheet Offer
desc: With limited runway remaining, an aggressive venture fund offers $250,000 in emergency funding, but demands 35% equity and 2 board veto seats.

A.title: Accept Term Sheet to Guarantee Survival
A.log: Accepted the predatory term sheet. Solved the immediate cash crisis with +$250k, but surrendered significant strategic board control.

B.title: Reject Offer & Commit to Wartime Bootstrapping
B.log: Rejected the predatory term sheet. The team rallied in wartime mode, determined to reach profitability independently.

title: Viral AI Influencer Endorsement
desc: A prominent AI tech influencer posted a glowing organic review of your startup on YouTube and X, causing a massive surge of 25,000 signups.

A.title: Scale Cloud Tier Immediately ($4,000)
A.log: Scaled cloud servers dynamically to absorb the viral traffic! Converted thousands of trial users and unlocked +$8,000 MRR!

B.title: Throttle Signups with a VIP Waitlist
B.log: Introduced an exclusive waitlist. Protected server stability and created strong artificial scarcity among enterprise buyers.

title: Researcher Discloses an API Vulnerability
desc: An independent security researcher emails you privately: your API leaks customer records to any authenticated account. She gives you 30 days before public disclosure.

A.title: Pay the Bounty & Patch in the Open
A.log: Paid the bounty, patched inside a week, and published the post-mortem. Enterprise buyers now cite your disclosure policy in their security reviews.

B.title: Quietly Patch & Say Nothing
B.log: Patched silently and never disclosed. The researcher published anyway. Two enterprise deals stalled in security review and churn climbed.

title: Data Protection Audit Lands
desc: A regulator opens a routine data-protection audit. Your data retention policy was written in a weekend and has never been reviewed by counsel.

A.title: Engage Counsel & Remediate Properly
A.log: Brought in real counsel and rebuilt the retention policy. Expensive, but the audit closed clean and enterprise procurement got easier.

B.title: Answer It Yourself Over a Weekend
B.log: Answered the audit yourself at 3am for two weeks. It closed with findings, and you have not slept properly since.

title: Your Best Engineer Gets an Offer
desc: A large tech company offers your strongest engineer double her salary. She tells you before accepting, which is itself a sign of how much she wants to stay.

A.title: Counter with Cash You Do Not Have
A.log: Countered hard and she stayed. The team saw you fight for someone, and it cost you a month of runway.

B.title: Let Her Go Well & Keep the Relationship
B.log: Wished her well and wrote the reference yourself. The team understood, but her half of the codebase is now nobody's.

title: Enterprise Pilot with a Brutal Requirement
desc: A large enterprise wants a paid pilot. They need one feature your product does not have, and it is six weeks of work that no other customer will ever use.

A.title: Build It & Take the Logo
A.log: Built the bespoke feature and landed the logo. The revenue is real and so is the six weeks of code only one customer will ever touch.

B.title: Decline & Stay on Roadmap
B.log: Turned down the pilot and kept the roadmap intact. Painful in the moment, and the product stayed one product.

title: You Have Not Taken a Day Off in Four Months
desc: Your co-founder pulls you aside. You have been short with the team, you missed two obvious bugs last week, and you cannot remember the last full night of sleep.

A.title: Take a Real Week Off
A.preview: Cash -$2,000 | Clarity +30% | MRR flat for a week
A.log: Took a genuine week off and left your laptop closed. Nothing burned down. You came back able to read your own numbers again.

B.title: Push Through to the Next Milestone
B.log: Pushed through. You hit the milestone and paid for it in judgment, and the team started routing around you.

title: A Customer Asks to Prepay a Year
desc: Your largest customer offers to prepay twelve months up front in exchange for a 30% discount. It solves this quarter and costs you next year.

A.title: Take the Cash Now
A.log: Took the prepayment. Runway extended dramatically, and you sold next year's revenue at a discount to survive this one.

B.title: Hold the Price & Stay Monthly
B.log: Held the line on price. The revenue quality stayed clean and the cash crunch stayed exactly where it was.

title: Board meeting
desc: Every 12 weeks the board reviews the target you committed to and sets a new one (grow MRR, cut burn, or reach fit).

B.title: Push back with your own plan

title: Tariq wants to talk
desc: He says he's doing half the work for none of the credit, and he's not sure he still believes in the plan.

A.title: More equity and the CTO title, publicly

B.title: Tell him the plan isn't changing

title: Nour asks you to choose
desc: "I'm not asking you to quit. I'm asking whether there's still room for us in this." Nour has packed a bag for the weekend, for two.
